```{r}
})
```

# Equal weights approach to index
```{r}
# ----------- 1. Rescale Raster Layers to 0–100 -----------
rescale_0_100 <- function(r) {
  min_val <- terra::global(r, fun = "min", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
  max_val <- terra::global(r, fun = "max", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
  (r - min_val) / (max_val - min_val) * 100
}

# Assuming 'aligned_rasters' is already a named list of 10x10m SpatRasters
vuln_stack_scaled <- lapply(aligned_rasters, rescale_0_100)
vuln_stack_scaled <- rast(vuln_stack_scaled)

# ----------- 2. Create Direct Vulnerability Index (Equal Weights) -----------
weights <- rep(1, nlyr(vuln_stack_scaled))
VI_direct_raster <- terra::weighted.mean(vuln_stack_scaled, w = weights, na.rm = TRUE)
names(VI_direct_raster) <- "VI_direct"

VI_direct_raster_scaled <- rescale_0_100(VI_direct_raster)
names(VI_direct_raster_scaled) <- "VI_direct_scaled"

# ----------- 3. Quintile Classification into 5 Vulnerability Levels -----------
quantile_breaks <- quantile(values(VI_direct_raster_scaled), probs = seq(0, 1, 0.2), na.rm = TRUE)

VI_direct_class <- classify(VI_direct_raster_scaled, rcl = matrix(c(
  -Inf, quantile_breaks[2], 1,
  quantile_breaks[2], quantile_breaks[3], 2,
  quantile_breaks[3], quantile_breaks[4], 3,
  quantile_breaks[4], quantile_breaks[5], 4,
  quantile_breaks[5], Inf, 5
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE))

# Convert to factor with labels
VI_direct_class <- as.factor(VI_direct_class)
levels(VI_direct_class) <- data.frame(
  value = 1:5,
  label = c(
    "Very Low Vulnerability",
    "Low Vulnerability",
    "Vulnerable",
    "Moderately Vulnerable",
    "Highly Vulnerable"
  )
)

# ----------- 4. Plot with Administrative Boundaries -----------
plot_direct_parishes_index <- ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = VI_direct_class, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_spatvector(data = Adm_boundaries, color = "black", fill = NA) +
  geom_spatvector_text(data = Adm_boundaries, aes(label = PName2016), 
                       size = 3, color = "black", check_overlap = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Very Low Vulnerability" = "#1a9850",
      "Low Vulnerability" = "#66bd63",
      "Vulnerable" = "#ffffbf",
      "Moderately Vulnerable" = "#fdae61",
      "Highly Vulnerable" = "#d7191c"
    ),
    name = "Vulnerability Scale",
    na.value = "transparent"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Malnutrition Vulnerability Index - Quintile Classification",
    subtitle = "Computed using Equal Weights Approach",
    caption = "Source: WorldPop Development Indicators | Method: Direct Vulnerability Index (VIdirect)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),

    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey80"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  ) +
```

# PCA Analysis
```{r}
# #################### Step 1: Convert Rasters to Dataframe ####################
# Convert aligned SpatRaster objects into a single raster stack
vulnerability_stack <- rast(aligned_rasters)

df <- as.data.frame(vulnerability_stack, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)

# Store XY coordinates separately
xy_coords <- df[, c("x", "y")]

# Remove XY coordinates from the dataframe before analysis
df <- df[, !(colnames(df) %in% c("x", "y"))]

# #################### Step 2: Visualize Outliers Using Boxplots ####################
# boxplot(df, main = "Boxplots of Variables")  

# #################### Step 3: Perform KMO Test and Remove Low-MSA Variables ####################
perform_kmo <- function(df, max_iterations = 10) {
  iteration <- 0
  thresholds <- seq(0.1, 0.5, by = 0.1)  # Gradually increase the threshold
  removed_vars_summary <- list()  # To store removed variables for each threshold

  for (threshold in thresholds) {
    removed_vars <- c()  # Track removed variables for the current threshold
    repeat {
      kmo_results <- KMO(df)
      print(kmo_results)

      message("Iteration: ", iteration, " | Threshold: ", threshold)
      print(kmo_results$MSAi)

      if (all(kmo_results$MSAi >= threshold)) break

      vars_to_remove <- names(kmo_results$MSAi)[kmo_results$MSAi < threshold]
      df <- df[, !(colnames(df) %in% vars_to_remove)]

      message("Removing variables with MSAi < ", threshold, ": ", paste(vars_to_remove, collapse = ", "))
      removed_vars <- c(removed_vars, vars_to_remove)

      iteration <- iteration + 1
      if (iteration >= max_iterations) break
    }
    removed_vars_summary[[as.character(threshold)]] <- removed_vars
  }

  # Print summary of removed variables
  message("Summary of removed variables:")
  for (threshold in names(removed_vars_summary)) {
    message("Threshold ", threshold, ": ", paste(removed_vars_summary[[threshold]], collapse = ", "))
  }

  return(df)
}

# Apply KMO filtering
df <- perform_kmo(df)

# #################### Step 4: Compute Correlation Matrix ####################
cor_matrix <- cor(df, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
print(cor_matrix)
# Generate correlation heatmap
ggcorrplot(
  cor_matrix,
  method = "circle",
  type = "lower",
  lab = TRUE,
  lab_size = 3,
  colors = c("#6D9EC1", "white", "#E46726"),
  title = "Correlation Heatmap of Variables",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal()
)

# Conduct Bartlett's test for sphericity (ensures PCA is valid)
bartlett_test <- cortest.bartlett(cor_matrix, n = nrow(df))
print(bartlett_test)

# #################### Step 5: Check Multicollinearity ####################
# Check determinant of correlation matrix (should not be close to 0)
det_value <- det(cor_matrix)
print(det_value)  

# Compute Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) to detect multicollinearity
df <- as.data.frame(df)  # Convert to data frame

vif_values <- sapply(names(df), function(var) {
  predictors <- setdiff(names(df), var)
  lm_model <- lm(as.formula(paste(var, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = "+"))), data = df)
  return(vif(lm_model))
})
print(vif_values)

remove_high_vif_iteratively <- function(df, threshold = 5) {
  current_df <- df
  removed_vars <- c()

  repeat {
    # Bereken VIF per variabele (zoals in collinearity-analyse)
    vif_model <- lm(as.matrix(current_df) ~ 1)  # placeholder
    vif_values <- NULL

    # Iteratief elke predictor als afhankelijke variabele
    vif_values <- sapply(names(current_df), function(var) {
      predictors <- setdiff(names(current_df), var)
      model <- lm(current_df[[var]] ~ ., data = current_df[, predictors, drop = FALSE])
      r2 <- summary(model)$r.squared
      if (is.na(r2)) return(Inf)
      return(1 / (1 - r2))
    })

    max_vif <- max(vif_values, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (max_vif < threshold) break

    var_to_remove <- names(vif_values)[which.max(vif_values)]
    removed_vars <- c(removed_vars, var_to_remove)
    cat(sprintf("Removing variable '%s' with VIF %.2f\n", var_to_remove, max_vif))

    current_df <- current_df[, !(names(current_df) %in% var_to_remove)]
  }

  if (length(removed_vars) == 0) {
    cat("No variables were removed. All VIF values are acceptable.\n")
  } else {
    cat("Removed variables due to high VIFs:", paste(removed_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }

  return(current_df)
}

df <- remove_high_vif_iteratively(df, threshold = 5)

# #################### Step 6: Conduct PCA with Oblimin Rotation and Kaiser Normalization ####################
# Run PCA with oblimin rotation and Kaiser normalization
pca_result_1 <- principal(df, 
              nfactors = 1,    # Choose based on eigenvalues >1 or scree plot
              rotate = "varimax", 
              scores = TRUE, 
              normalize = TRUE) # Applies Kaiser normalization

# Print PCA results
print(pca_result_1)

pca_result_2 <- principal(df, 
              nfactors = 2, 
              rotate = "varimax", 
              scores = TRUE, 
              normalize = TRUE)

print(pca_result_2)

pca_result_3 <- principal(df, 
              nfactors = 3, 
              rotate = "varimax", 
              scores = TRUE, 
              normalize = TRUE)

print(pca_result_3)

eigenvalues <- eigen(cor(df))$values
print(eigenvalues)

# Scree plot
plot(eigenvalues, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Principal Component",
     ylab = "Eigenvalue",
     main = "Scree Plot of PCA") %>%
abline(h = 1, col = "red", lty = 2)

# Merge XY coordinates back to the PCA scores
pca_scores_with_xy <- cbind(xy_coords, as.data.frame(pca_result_3$scores))

# Convert PCA scores back into a raster stack
pca_raster <- rast(pca_scores_with_xy)

autoplot(pca_raster, main = "PCA Scores (3 Components)")

```

## Computing the PCA-based index
```{r}
# ----- 1. Define weights for PCA components -----
weights <- c(0.29, 0.37, 0.34)  # Based on explained variance of PC1–PC3

# ----- 2. Compute weighted PCA index -----
pca_index <- (weights[1] * pca_result_3$scores[, 1]) +
             (weights[2] * pca_result_3$scores[, 2]) +
             (weights[3] * pca_result_3$scores[, 3])

# ----- 3. Rescale PCA index to 0–100 -----
rescale_0_100_vector <- function(x) {
  (x - min(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / (max(x, na.rm = TRUE) - min(x, na.rm = TRUE)) * 100
}

pca_index_scaled <- rescale_0_100_vector(pca_index)

# ----- 4. Create data frame and raster -----
pca_index_df <- data.frame(xy_coords, pca_index_scaled)
names(pca_index_df)[3] <- "pca_index"

# Convert back to raster
pca_index_raster <- rast(pca_index_df, crs = crs(KAMP_POPULATION_10m))
names(pca_index_raster) <- "PCA_Index"

# ----- 5. Classify into 5 quantiles (Likert scale) -----
quantile_breaks <- quantile(pca_index_df$pca_index, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 6), na.rm = TRUE)

pca_index_df$quantile <- cut(
  pca_index_df$pca_index,
  breaks = quantile_breaks,
  labels = FALSE,
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

# Convert quantile column to raster
pca_quantile_raster <- rast(pca_index_df[, c("x", "y", "quantile")])
pca_quantile_raster <- as.factor(pca_quantile_raster)

# ----- 6. Define fill scale and labels -----
likert_colors <- c(
  "1" = "#1a9850",   # Very Low Vulnerability
  "2" = "#66bd63",   # Low Vulnerability
  "3" = "#ffffbf",   # Vulnerable
  "4" = "#fdae61",   # Moderately Vulnerable
  "5" = "#d7191c"    # Highly Vulnerable
)

likert_labels <- c(
  "1" = "Very Low Vulnerability",
  "2" = "Low Vulnerability",
  "3" = "Vulnerable",
  "4" = "Moderately Vulnerable",
  "5" = "Highly Vulnerable"
)

# ----- 7. Plot PCA-Based Vulnerability Index with Administrative Boundaries -----
plot_quantile_parishes_index <- ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = pca_quantile_raster, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_spatvector(data = Adm_boundaries, color = "black", fill = NA) +
  geom_spatvector_text(
    data = Adm_boundaries,
    aes(label = PName2016),
    size = 3, color = "black", check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = likert_colors,
    labels = likert_labels,
    name = "Vulnerability Scale",
    na.value = "transparent"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA-Based Vulnerability Index (Likert Scale)",
    subtitle = "Based on Rescaled Weighted PCA Components (0–100)",
    caption = "Source: WorldPop Development Indicators | Method: PCA (3 components, weighted)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1, size = 9),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey80"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(na.translate = FALSE)))

# ----- 8. Display the final map -----
plot_quantile_parishes_index
```

# Difference between Direct and PCA-based indices
```{r}
# ----------------- 1. Align the two rasters -----------------
pca_index_aligned <- Spatial.align::align(pca_index_raster, VI_direct_raster_scaled, resample_method = "near")

# ----------------- 2. Compute the difference raster -----------------
index_diff_raster <- pca_index_aligned - VI_direct_raster_scaled
names(index_diff_raster) <- "Index_Difference"

# ----------------- 3. Plot the difference raster -----------------
# Compute max absolute difference for symmetrical scaling around 0
diff_vals <- values(index_diff_raster)
diff_range <- max(abs(diff_vals), na.rm = TRUE)

# Plot: Green (lower), White (neutral), Red (higher)
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = index_diff_raster, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_spatvector(data = Adm_boundaries, color = "black", fill = NA) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#1a9850",      # Green = Direct Index higher
    mid = "white",        # Neutral = Equal
    high = "#d7191c",     # Red = PCA Index higher
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-diff_range, diff_range),
    name = "Index Difference\n(PCA - Direct)",
    na.value = "transparent"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Difference Between PCA-Based and Direct Vulnerability Index",
    subtitle = "Green = Direct Index Higher | Red = PCA Index Higher | White = Agreement"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey80"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey90"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(barwidth = 1, barheight = 20))

# ----------------- 4. Categorized version -----------------
# Create classification matrix
reclass_matrix <- matrix(c(
  -Inf, -50, 1,
  -50, -30, 2,
  -30, -10, 3,
  -10,  10, 4,   # Agreement zone
   10,  30, 5,
   30,  50, 6,
   50,  Inf, 7
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# Classify the difference raster
index_diff_class <- classify(index_diff_raster, rcl = reclass_matrix)

# Convert to factor with interpretable labels
index_diff_class <- as.factor(index_diff_class)

levels(index_diff_class) <- data.frame(
  value = 1:7,
  label = c(
    "Much Higher (Direct, >50 points)",    # 1
    "Higher (Direct, 30–50 points)",       # 2
    "Slightly Higher (Direct, 10–30 points)", # 3
    "Agreement (±10 points)",             # 4
    "Slightly Higher (PCA, 10–30 points)", # 5
    "Higher (PCA, 30–50 points)",         # 6
    "Much Higher (PCA, >50 points)"       # 7
  )
)

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = index_diff_class, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_spatvector(data = Adm_boundaries, color = "black", fill = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Much Higher (Direct, >50 points)" = "#00441b",
      "Higher (Direct, 30–50 points)" = "#238b45",
      "Slightly Higher (Direct, 10–30 points)" = "#66c2a4",
      "Agreement (±10 points)" = "#ffffcc",
      "Slightly Higher (PCA, 10–30 points)" = "#fdbb84",
      "Higher (PCA, 30–50 points)" = "#e34a33",
      "Much Higher (PCA, >50 points)" = "#990000"
    ),
    name = "Index Difference",
    na.value = "transparent"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Classified Difference Between PCA-Based and Direct Vulnerability Index",
    subtitle = "Based on 7 Class Scale | Centered at Agreement",
    caption = "Negative classes reflect higher vulnerability from the Direct Index;\nPositive classes from the PCA Index; Agreement indicates minimal difference."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
    subtitle = "Based on 7 Class Scale | Centered at Agreement",
    caption = "Negative classes reflect higher vulnerability from the Direct Index;\nPositive classes from the PCA Index; Agreement indicates minimal difference."
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(na.translate = FALSE)))

# Combine the PCA and Direct index rasters into a single SpatRaster
index_combined <- c(pca_index_aligned, VI_direct_raster_scaled)

# Compute the Pearson correlation using terra's layerCor
correlation_result <- terra::layerCor(index_combined, fun = "cor", na.rm = TRUE)

# Print the result
print(correlation_result)

# ----------------- 5. Density Plot of Scaled Values -----------------
# Combine into one data frame
# Make sure both rasters are aligned
VI_direct_vals <- as.vector(values(VI_direct_raster_scaled))
PCA_vals_scaled <- as.vector(pca_index_scaled)

# Drop NAs for fair comparison
valid_idx <- which(!is.na(VI_direct_vals) & !is.na(PCA_vals_scaled))
direct_vals <- VI_direct_vals[valid_idx]
pca_vals <- PCA_vals_scaled[valid_idx]

density_df <- data.frame(
  Index_Value = c(direct_vals, pca_vals),
  Index_Type = rep(c("Direct Index", "PCA-Based Index"), each = length(valid_idx))
)

# Plot
ggplot(density_df, aes(x = Index_Value, fill = Index_Type, color = Index_Type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Direct Index" = "#1a9850", "PCA-Based Index" = "#d7191c")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Direct Index" = "#1a9850", "PCA-Based Index" = "#d7191c")) +
  labs(
    title = "Density Plot of Vulnerability Indices (Scaled 0–100)",
    subtitle = "Comparison Between Direct Index and PCA-Based Index",
    x = "Index Value (0–100)",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Index Type",
    color = "Index Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )

# ----------------- 6. Misclassification Analysis using the vulnerability categories -----------------
crs(pca_quantile_raster) <- "EPSG:32636"
crs(VI_direct_class) <- "EPSG:32636"

pca_quantile_aligned <- Spatial.align::align(pca_quantile_raster, VI_direct_class, resample_method = "near")

# stack the two rasters
quantile_df <- c(pca_quantile_aligned, VI_direct_class)

# Convert to data frame for comparison
quantile_df <- as.data.frame(quantile_df, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)

# Drop rows where either index is NA
quantile_df <- na.omit(quantile_df)

# rename columns for clarity
colnames(quantile_df) <- c("x", "y", "pca_class", "direct_class")

# Define labels in correct order
vulnerability_levels <- c(
  "Very Low Vulnerability",
  "Low Vulnerability",
  "Vulnerable",
  "Moderately Vulnerable",
  "Highly Vulnerable"
)

# Convert pca_class from numeric to labeled factor
quantile_df$pca_class <- factor(
  as.numeric(quantile_df$pca_class),
  levels = 1:5,
  labels = vulnerability_levels
)

# Convert direct_class to a factor with the same level order
quantile_df$direct_class <- factor(
  quantile_df$direct_class,
  levels = vulnerability_levels
)

# Now generate the confusion matrix
conf_matrix <- caret::confusionMatrix(quantile_df$pca_class, quantile_df$direct_class)

print(conf_matrix)

# Compute directional difference
directional_diff_raster <- pca_quantile_aligned - VI_direct_class
names(directional_diff_raster) <- "Directional_Misclassification"

# Convert to factor with interpretation
directional_diff_factor <- as.factor(directional_diff_raster)

levels(directional_diff_factor) <- data.frame(
  value = -4:4,
  label = c(
    "-4 - PCA much lower (4-class underestimation)",      # Very Low vs. Highly Vulnerable
    "-3 - PCA substantially lower (3-class underestimation)",
    "-2 - PCA lower (2-class underestimation)",
    "-1 - PCA slightly lower (1-class underestimation)",
    "0 - Full agreement",
    "1 - PCA slightly higher (1-class overestimation)",
    "2 - PCA higher (2-class overestimation)",
    "3 - PCA substantially higher (3-class overestimation)",
    "4 - PCA much higher (4-class overestimation)"         # Highly Vulnerable vs. Very Low
  )
)

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = directional_diff_factor, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_spatvector(data = Adm_boundaries, color = "black", fill = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "-4 - PCA much lower (4-class underestimation)" = "#2166ac",
      "-3 - PCA substantially lower (3-class underestimation)" = "#67a9cf",
      "-2 - PCA lower (2-class underestimation)" = "#d1e5f0",
      "-1 - PCA slightly lower (1-class underestimation)" = "#e0f3f8",
      "0 - Full agreement" = "#f7f7f7",
      "1 - PCA slightly higher (1-class overestimation)" = "#fddbc7",
      "2 - PCA higher (2-class overestimation)" = "#f4a582",
      "3 - PCA substantially higher (3-class overestimation)" = "#d6604d",
      "4 - PCA much higher (4-class overestimation)" = "#b2182b"
    ),
    name = "Misclassification Type",
    na.value = "transparent",
    na.translate = FALSE  # <-- this removes NA from the legend
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Directional Misclassification Map",
    subtitle = "Signed Difference in Vulnerability Classification (PCA - Direct)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm"),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    legend.spacing.y = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9)
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(
      title = "Misclassification Type",
      ncol = 2
    )
  )

# Add agreement indicator
quantile_df$agreement <- quantile_df$pca_class == quantile_df$direct_class

# Bar chart
ggplot(quantile_df, aes(x = direct_class, fill = agreement)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = "#1a9850", "FALSE" = "#d7191c"),
    labels = c("Agreement", "Disagreement"),
    name = "Agreement"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Agreement Rate Per Vulnerability Class",
    subtitle = "Proportion of Agreement by Direct Index Level",
    x = "Direct Vulnerability Level",
    y = "Proportion"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5)
  )

table_df <- as.data.frame(table(quantile_df$direct_class, quantile_df$pca_class))
colnames(table_df) <- c("Direct", "PCA", "Freq")

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define the class order
# ----------------------------------------------------
vulnerability_levels <- c(
  "Very Low Vulnerability",
  "Low Vulnerability",
  "Vulnerable",
  "Moderately Vulnerable",
  "Highly Vulnerable"
)

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 2. Ensure factors are in the right order for axes
# ----------------------------------------------------
table_df <- table_df %>%
  mutate(
    Direct = factor(Direct, levels = rev(vulnerability_levels)),  # Y-axis (top-down)
    PCA = factor(PCA, levels = vulnerability_levels),             # X-axis (left-right)
    Agreement = Direct == PCA                                     # Logical indicator for diagonal
  )

# ----------------------------------------------------
# 4. Plot the heatmap with emphasis on diagonal (agreement)
# ----------------------------------------------------
# Filter out rows and columns where Direct or PCA is NA
table_df <- table_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(Direct) & !is.na(PCA))

ggplot(table_df, aes(x = PCA, y = Direct, fill = Freq)) +
geom_tile(color = ifelse(table_df$Agreement, "black", "white"), size = 0.6) +
geom_text(
    aes(label = Freq, fontface = ifelse(!is.na(Agreement) & Agreement, "bold", "plain")),
    size = 3, color = "black"
  ) +
scale_fill_viridis_c(
  option = "B",
  begin = 0.2, end = 0.95,
  name = "Frequency"
) +
labs(
  title = "Cross-Class Frequency Heatmap",
  subtitle = "Comparison of PCA and Direct Vulnerability Classes (Scaled 1–5)",
  x = "PCA Class",
  y = "Direct Class",
  caption = paste0(
    "Diagonal cells represent agreement in classification.\n",
    "Bold values indicate matched vulnerability categories (e.g., 'Highly Vulnerable' in both indices)."
  )
) +
theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
theme(
  plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
  axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
  axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
  legend.position = "right",
  legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
  plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0)
)
```
